correctness.rationale: For every integer \(m\ge1\) and infection rate \(\lambda>0\), condition on the \(\operatorname{Exp}(1)\) lifetime \(T\) of the common hub. On a triangle, \(p_0=e^{-2\lambda T}\) and \(p_1=2(e^{-\lambda T}-e^{-2\lambda T})/(1+\lambda)\); the latter includes contagion after hub recovery via \(\mathbb E[e^{-\lambda E}]=1/(1+\lambda)\) for an independent unit exponential \(E\). Given \(T\), independent edge/recovery clocks make triangle outcomes i.i.d.; \(U=e^{-\lambda T}\) is beta-distributed with moments \(\mathbb E[U^k]=1/(1+k\lambda)\). Exact moments give the finite variance difference \(D_m=-\lambda^2Q_m/[2m(1+\lambda)^4(1+2\lambda)^2(1+3\lambda)(1+4\lambda)]\). The polynomial \(Q_m\) has coefficient signs \(+,+,-,-,-,-\) in descending order and exactly one positive root by Descartes' rule. The strictly decreasing thresholds follow from \(D_m=D_\infty+B/m\), with \(B>0\). Independent labeled-state CTMC recursions for one through four triangles and three rates match all coefficients of the integrated generating functions; 95 exact checks passed. The all-size claim relies on analytic proof, not finite calculations.

value.rationale: This is a natural epidemic clustering comparison: add exactly one edge inside each of \(m\) disjoint leaf pairs while keeping the hub and vertex count fixed. The mean infection fraction increases at every rate, while the final-size variance reverses sign exactly once for every finite graph. The thresholds decrease strictly from \(1+\sqrt2\) to the unique positive root \(1.07327153\ldots\) of an explicit quartic. The full finite generating function and the non-self-averaging beta-transformed limit explain the mechanism. This is a motivated complete classification across an infinite graph family rather than an arbitrary isolated calculation.
risks: Relevance is a mathematical benchmark for a stylized graph, not a direct empirical disease forecast.
